notes.title: Beta Build: Performance Update
notes.content:
[p]So...its been a long journey for this update. Frankly far too long and its been the most difficult thing I've ever had to code, and its still far from finished. Honestly, I was close to giving up and reverting this update multiple times because there where points where despite literally months of hard and stressful work I was seeing the same FPS as the currently live build.

I've decided what I will do is post it to the Beta branch but[b] I[/b] [b]do not recommend[/b] anyone tries to use it to play Aiyana. Instead its there if anyone is curious to check on my progress or if you are more tech savvy you can profile it to see exactly what is changing.

I'm doing this to be open. So you can see the state of what I'm working on and try to get a sense of why its taking so long. I feel like I've been saying the equivalent of "trust me bro" for a while now and to be honest its putting a lot of pressure on me.

I can see the potential with these techniques, but its taking so long to rework almost every aspect of Aiyana to hook into them and since I've already spent so much time on this, it feels like I should power through and get it finished.

To put things in perspective, this is the current default draw distance in Aiyana:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/866aa95d319a7f968cc0e78d4789151f826afd54.png"][/img][/p][p]This pic was taken whilst up high so its purposely a bit of an extreme example to help explain my point. This next image is what I'm aiming for:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/f83df0f243462f499f953441c760e6190e07dc13.png"][/img]
The difference is pretty huge and helps the world feel much more expansive. It will also influence gameplay and give a good reason to climb a mountain so you can spot those rarer biomes and feel like you are exploring rather than stumbling around hoping to find things.

So despite it taking so long, it feels like this is important enough to justify the time and it not just me ticking the box of "other games in the genre can do this, I should be able to as well". Although in my defence a lot of the artistic decisions in Aiyana do make this more difficult (E.G real trees instead of cubes).

For anyone that does want to have a look at the beta here are a list of caveats to look out for:
[/p][list][*][p]Fish and flying insects have been disabled[/p][/*][*][p]Existing worlds may load with a seed corruption (as though two different worlds have mixed)[/p][/*][*][p]Clouds don't look as nice and their shadows render strangely when looking from below[/p][/*][*][p]There is a flickering with the main terrain rendering, which is worse at higher distances[/p][/*][*][p]If you look around quickly at a low FPS, you will see gaps on the edges of the screen[/p][/*][*][p]Controller support has been added to a ton more things, however this was done by a contractor who didn't have the best attention to detail that has resulted in some mouse/keyboard interactions being utterly broken. Ive found and fixed a few, but not had a chance to check everything he changed yet[/p][/*][*][p]Cave generation has changed and vines have been added but occasionally rendering will utterly stop whilst exploring them[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]My intention is that by releasing in such a raw state I can take the pressure off myself a bit and share updates more regularly as I make more incremental progress towards the end goal instead of me aiming to deliver something people can use right away. [/p][p][/p][p]E.G I can now aim for the next update to be something like "Fish are working again" instead of "Everything is done"[/p]

notes.title: Progress Update: Performance Pt. 2
notes.content:
*TLDR, another very technical and dry post about performance ahead! I'm playing with different techniques that could potentially double draw distances. Still not sure when it will be done*

I'm still busy on these huge performance changes and, well its been a ride to say the least!

Since my last post, Cubic Worlds released so I gave their demo a try and I have to say, their draw distance is impressive. It made me realise I must be doing something fundamentally wrong and so I went back and checked over techniques I had tried in the past to see if I was missing something.

Turns out, I did do something wrong when I was testing an early technique around instancing.

What I explained in my last post around graphics cards being better around processing large chunks of information, where a bigger chunk is quicker to render than 4 smaller chunks, can be leveraged in a unique way. Say you want to render, 100,000 cubes. Your graphics card will struggle with this because for each cube, it needs to do things like make sure its mesh, texture, materials etc are ready to be used.

Hence why combining chunks saves time because it will reduce the time spent preparing for each draw.

However if you utilise something called instancing (a common technique already used extensively in Aiyana and most games) then you effectively tell the graphics card, "I am about to render a lot of the same thing, skip all your usual checks".

So what I'm now doing is instead of expressing the world as complex meshes, it is expressed entirely as cubes and rendered using instancing. 

I had tried this in the past but it was so long ago I'm not sure what I would have missed to dismiss the technique. For example I have a technique called Greedy Meshing which lets me scan a chunk and combine the same blocks into the same face, which I was able to rewrite to combine into the same cubes instead of faces. Perhaps my first tests of instancing didn't have greedy meshing yet. Anyway, doing this cuts down on how many cubes are needed to render very drastically and combining this with the Occlusion Culling technique mentioned in the last post, worlds can be expressed in a sensible number of cubes. 

However it now means that Occlusion Culling was a bit primitive since it was running on sections of 16x16x16 blocks, but since I'm not trying to combine into a mesh and instead can link specific cubes to an Occlusion group, it means I could rewrite OC to be more dynamic and thus more efficient. So instead of arbitarily trying to join 16 block sections together, it can now scan to the exact height of each cave and so entire cave sections can be disabled instead of partial sections.

So now I can express worlds as a sensible number of cubes and it has exposed some interesting other problems to solve! For example, this means I'm now processing and trying to prepare 100,000+ cubes for rendering every frame. Which is just a Lot of data to be moving around and since I'm working in Unity+Burst it means I can't use traditional techniques for storing/accessing large arrays of data and had to get creative with pointers to get Occlusion Culling to even work.

Once all this data was prepared in an effecient way, I then need to send the changes to the graphics card and that would take a bit of time so I looked into how to improve this and found that Unity has a new-ish technique for writing directly to memory on the graphics card, but to utilise it I had to rewrite how everything in the game that uses instancing (a ton of things) processes their memory.

Now that I have done that, it turns out that by writing to GPU memory directly requires really careful control of when/how you write that data, otherwise your CPU sits and waits on the GPU and vice versa. Which is what I'm trying to solve today.

So its been a bit of a trip! I've rewrote a lot of things and hopefully now the end is closer in sight. Its hard to predict how long this will take since each time I turn a corner, I've had to learn something new in order to solve a problem I didn't expect. I've also not had as much time to work on Aiyana this past couple of weeks but surely now its not That much more work to get this working... right? (On a serious note, it does feel like I'm getting close with all this).

notes.title: Progress Update: Performance + Caves
notes.content:
Since its been a couple of weeks and I'm still not sure when I'll be done with this next update I thought I should give a progress update. As forewarning, this one will be more technical than most in effort to explain why its taking so long.

I wanted to go back to a performance feature I mentioned a while back around occlusion culling, and since there are more animals now it felt like a good time to try it one more time. I've made enough progress now that I'm feeling more hopeful I can deliver on it and if all goes well, it should see about a 25% decrease in overall rendering times.

What I'm working on is sort of like this:
https://tomcc.github.io/2014/08/31/visibility-1.html

How graphics cards work is that they are Much more effecient processing big chunks of data instead of lots of little bits, so to lean into this strength Aiyana utilises something sort of like static batching, which is where once chunks load they look around their neighbours and start combining their meshes into larger versions. So instead of rendering 4 small chunk meshes, they are combined and 1 is rendered instead.

This is already in and works really well, the problem is that when I first attempted to implement occlusion culling, like in that link above, that it means disabling the static batching and the results where almost identical for perfomance. So it felt a bit pointless to trade an already working system for a different system that gives similar results.

So what I'm doing now is mixing the two systems, which is complex to say the least. I'm using my custom static batching for the meshes above ground which will receive almost no benefit from culling anyway. Then for meshes below ground, occlusion culling kicks in and the smaller meshes are disabled depending on what you can see.

It looks like I have a foundation working ok but I still have the time consuming edge cases to work out. What has made me stop and write this post is that the algorithms I use for caves are problematic for the culling algorithm. Too many of them are connected together by tiny tunnels so when I'm trying to detect what should render, too much is passing the checks to say "chunk X can travel and reach chunk Y".

As a result, I'm reworking the caves to find a better balance of nice visuals whilst also not being a drain on performance. Current caves are a bit narrow too often so my aim is to have more open caverns that are easier to explore/fight in.

notes.title: Deer
notes.content:
I've wanted to see a Deer in Aiyana for a long time, in fact I first bought their animations back in 2018! So it felt a bit overdue to get them into the world.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/78a895c1cabb67b8af3c9d0e7bb191f1c8ac633c.png[/img]

Of course as with most of the wildlife in Aiyana it becomes corrupted and much more dangerous at night

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/c4e2319be7487226165537840ac3c6de0368f770.png[/img]

During the day, Deer are quite elusive but at night they will hunt you down and charge without mercy. I was hoping that deer would fit into the exploding enemy category and as much as it felt cool to have them charge at you and explode, it also had various balancing issues and had to be dropped.

As a side note, the day version of the Deer can be tamed and 4 new cooking recipes have been added for Deer meat. FInally, Night Deer will now appear in challenges after wave 10.

[h3]Roadmap Update[/h3]
I'm still generally trying to focus on smaller updates at the moment, the next one will probably be some more controller support and polish/improvements to Ranching.

I'm trying to work towards Leatherworking/Carnivore taming and wanted the Deer in so there is a more complete picture of how things will all fit together.

However I'm also concious that having more animals is more strain on performance so I'm probably due a performance pass soon as well. We will see what wins in the end.

notes.title: Release 0.3.0.4
notes.content:
So before I get into what changed in this release I should probably mention that in the Ranching update I added some new blocks but forgot to mention them! The first boss also got a mini update and casts a new spell so he should be a touch more challenging now.

[h3]Roofing And Carpeted Steps[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/4311c8ea7630e421e7ab149ae2ab2bde69cc9f13.png[/img]

The carpeted steps are available in all wood and stone variations and their carpet can be dyed to the usual colours. There are also a couple of new roofing blocks, hay for a thatched style and traditional tiles that can be crafted from clay.

[h3]Release 0.3.0.3[/h3]
As mentioned previously this is me trying to focus on some smaller updates to make sure Ranching isn't causing any issues before moving onto the next bigger update. I'm still not sure what it will be yet but I have a few considerations.

[h3]Map Rework[/h3]
The map has had a complete rework for its under the hood tech. Previously it would store all its data into one large file but now its data is split into a file per region, which is how blocks are also stored.

Whilst doing this, I've reduced the data maps take to be at least 4x smaller than before.

Unfortunately though, this means [b]old map data is no longer compatible[/b] so your map will be blank. I did this because it wasn't going to be an easy/clean transfer of the data and it didn't feel important enough to justify the time spent when I could be fixing bugs or adding new features instead. Sorry for the inconvenience, I realise its not ideal.

[h3]Map Icon Highlighting[/h3]
Whilst I was working with the map it felt like a good time to add another QoL feature to it.

[previewyoutube=IzdJhkAz6iY;full][/previewyoutube]

Now as you  highlight icons in the Legend section it will dim other elements of the map to make things easier to spot

[h3]Backup Files[/h3]
I noticed whilst testing that backups can start to add up to a lot of storage taken in Steam Cloud and as a result, it could take a while to relaunch the game.

To fix this I've moved backup files from Steam Cloud and moved them into My Documents instead. This might mean it takes a bit longer to launch Aiyana for the first time with this update as its moving the files around but it should be much quicker after this.

[h3]World Save Files[/h3]
Whilst I was making the change to backups it seemed like a good time to make a change to other save files and get this all out of the way at the same time. So I've also updated the name of the files that store block data so they have a space in them. E.G "Region0,0.awd" will now be saved as "Region 0,0.awd"

What this means is that your old backups probably wont work out of the box until you rename the world files to match this change in naming convention.

notes.title: Progress Update
notes.content:
Ranching is coming along nicely but its a big feature and still a few weeks away so I wanted to give an update on the progress so far as well as a rough overview of how its taking shape.

Most of the core for Ranching is working in a basic form, I'm now in the slower refinement phase where I'm trying to hunt down all the bugs and edge case scenarios as well as making sure there are enough QoL features such as seeing tamed animals on the map.

Firstly, to tame an animal you craft a sleeping treat that you place on the floor. Once the animal has eaten enough of them, it falls asleep letting you put a collar on them. Larger animals need more treats than smaller ones and Collars are crafted from Leather Strips + Cotton.

Once tamed, you can feed your pets at the feed trough. Each feed takes different crop types and gives animals different stats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/cd44293160c227d28f469b3f87f1ab7197a10622.png[/img]

Animals have preferred food for different growth types. So one feed could increase Meat quality but reduce another quality such as Eggs, Milk or Fat.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/72e3bc9972a5389bf42fe116bbcbc6a0ca0493cd.png[/img]

Each pet will give you a buff and they can give more buffs as you increase their grade, which is done via breeding/feeding.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/da07436f7900874608939126c455b16307e5eeaa.png[/img]

Once you are ready to breed an animal, you need to craft an Incubator and Fertility Treats. It will list nearby animals and once selected the parents will walk to the incubator to produce a baby.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/370954877d5cdb0fb0bfe77757286e3249391583.png[/img]

Babies will need milk in order to grow into an adult that can be gathered from tamed Cows using a Pail. If you increase a cows milk quality, it will produce more each time you milk it.

Finally a small perk tree has been added for raising animals, it only has 4 perks for now but i plan to add more in the future when carnivores can be tamed as well.

notes.title: Spells Rework
notes.content:
Ironically, I first designed the spell controls for Aiyana with controllers in mind so it felt clunky on keyboards. So I remade them to cast using functions keys (F1 etc) and whilst it was better it still didn't feel great.

So i've decided to bite the bullet and rework spells again, this time so they act more like items and can be changed by pressing 1,2,3, scrolling the mouse wheel etc.

This change came about whilst I was balancing the infinite waves survival mode and during the more frantic waves I found I was pressing the wrong key more often than I would like because I wasn't used to pressing F1 etc compared to the usual number keys and mouse scrolling.

Hopefully, this change will have spells feeling a bit more natural whilst also solving the second hotbars feeling a bit superfluous since they can now be used to host additional spells.

[h3]Spells[/h3]
[list]
[*] Spells now act as items and cast on 1,2,3 instead of F1, F2, F3 etc
[*] Added a setting for single press spells, which will let you cast spells quicker (explained better in game)
[*] Spellbook screen has been redesigned, I've attempted to do so in a way that makes text much easier to read since the old version was pretty cramped
[*] Spellbook redesign now supports controller input
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/a88fdbdeaa1b7caa1decc4bcf2e5ebcde966de9c.png[/img]

[h3]Roadmap Update[/h3]
I've spent most of this month on bugs/small changes and made a good dent in the list of known issues so it feels like time to move back onto some new features since if I only fix bugs it will feel like Aiyana isn't growing.

Similarly, focusing on controller support will feel like dull updates for those that play on keyboard, who I suspect are the majority of Aiyanas players currently.

So I'm not entirely sure what will be best to tackle next. I have a couple of bigger features in mind but I'll need to experiment with them a little before I feel comfortable comitting to them.

[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Increased the minimum font size for the crafting UI in an effort to make it more legible

notes.title: Release 0.2.2.5
notes.content:
Mainly bug fixes and tweaks as I previously mentioned but some bigger changes crept their way in here as well:

[h3]Water[/h3]
Water has been reverted back to a simpler system that doesn't attempt to spread at all. The only time water will spread is if you break a block beside it and it will only replace that block.

I've done this for a few reasons. The first is that it will prevent seeing broken meshes and by not flowing/draining it means you wont see half empty rivers. The combination of these two factors didn't look great.

By using this simpler system the water meshes can benefit from all the same optimisations that chunk meshes have (greedy meshing, static batching) so as a bonus its far cheaper to render, especially since the meshes will be simpler.

[h3]Sprinting[/h3]
Sprinting has never felt quite right in how it levels up. By increasing speed a lot it can become hard to control but its not really feeling like its ticking the box I want which is that you can sprint for longer the more you play.

So to fit this goal, leveling up sprinting now reduces its stamina cost instead so you should be able to sprint for a lot longer.

I'm hoping that this also makes the enhanced sprint spell more meaninfgul since this spell gives that extra speed.

Finally, I've added an icon to show when you are sprinting or not to hopefully make that clearer.

[h3]Exploding Stone Elemental[/h3]
Stone Elementals will now explode on their death in quite a forgiving way. This is not intended to serve the usual purposes of an exploding enemy but adds an extra element of danger to their deaths.

notes.title: Challenges, Bears & Treants
notes.content:
It seems I made the coming soon post too early and got this update wrapped up sooner than expected. There have been some fairly significant changes and hopefully all of them for the better.

[h3]Challenges[/h3]
The biggest change is that challenges have been reworked to be infinite waves instead of a small subset of waves and rewards are new earned based on how many waves you managed to defeat. Most of the rewards are pretty similar to what was already on offer for challenges but there are a couple of new additions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/fd5c7513c784fd907ff6c5e6e24d1c629c4290c1.png[/img]

Once you finish a run you will earn experience based on your score and your highscore will be entered into a Leaderboard.

I've also sourced a full combat soundtrack for during the challenges to help set the tone properly for your imminent demise.

[h3]Treant[/h3]
The Treant is now in the world ready to squash unsuspecting players. He is a tough enemy so make sure you have plenty of bandages before taking one on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/e0d7028c656df1a4a87b447a24fbbe59d7a6f21e.png[/img]

His item drops are still up for debate, ideally I want him to drop something related to Enchanting but I'm not ready to work on that yet. For now he drops a Treant Heart which can be used to craft an improved Talisman for blocking magic damage.

[h3]Bears[/h3]
Bears are finally back in and wandering around the Mountain areas of Aiyana.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/23cd7e90e0a4cd38f73ea01dcfd8dd5d05a2634c.png[/img]

They are a tough enemy with lots of health but for now their item drops are still a work in progress. They drop the usual Leathers and Furs but currently don't have any extra purpose. This is because ultimately I want a better system for leather crafting so you can craft things like Bear Leather armour but its feeling like there are more important things to work on than Leatherworking right now.

This is why I delayed adding the bear for so long but I've added them now to make balancing the new challenges easier and to save having to keep rebalancing it as new enemies are added. I also just wanted a wider variety of animals wandering the world so it felt a shame to not have them.

[h3]New Font[/h3]
I've been trying to find a font for Aiyana that is both on theme for a tribal/nature based game whilst also being readable but it seems I'm chasing a unicorn so instead I've taken the plunge and replaced the font with one purely to be functional/readable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/3a74e2a2da33fc8bcf7e639dcdba5a53f6f96abf.png[/img]

It's not as interesting, but its undeniably easier to read so hopefully its a change for the better. To do this, I've had to check every bit of UI in the game and there is every chance I missed some so if you spot any text looking a little off please point it out!

[h3]Furnace & Composting Summaries[/h3]
This was a minor QoL update for Furnaces and Compost Bins to show a progress bar when you hover over them so you don't need to open them to check on progress.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/c750d5b41c0e363d8987a1427f0b12b7fa377c98.png[/img]

[h3]Roadmap Update[/h3]
I mentioned that I started on this update sooner than I should have so my intention for the next few patches is to go back to smaller ones and make tweaks for a bit. I did this because I've been trying to tick boxes in my head for a new trailer for the store page so I've been focused on getting in new content that has the potential to produce nice shots.

Now this update is ready, my aim is to spend a bit more time stabilising/improving what is already here, such as fixing issues with Water and possibly reverting it back to something simple. I've also not made progress towards controller support this patch and whilst testing for the challenges it really emphasized how much room there is to improve the animals A.I logic.

notes.title: Coming Soon: Treants & Bears
notes.content:
Now that the holidays are past I'm back in full swing and working on the next big update that should be ready in a few weeks time. In hindsight I shouldn't have started on this one as soon as I did and should have spent more time bug fixing the last update, something I'll try to keep in mind for the future.

[h3]Treant[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/e0d7028c656df1a4a87b447a24fbbe59d7a6f21e.png[/img]

The Treant will aim to be a mini boss within Aiyana with the aim of adding a little danger to exploring during the day. They should be fairly easy to avoid once you know what to look for so I'm not trying to impose on the more relaxed feeling of exploring but if you do take one on, you're in for a rough fight.

I've still not decided what loot the Treants will drop so aside from making sure its a good fight, new items will need to be made.

[h3]Bears[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/23cd7e90e0a4cd38f73ea01dcfd8dd5d05a2634c.png[/img]
Bears have been mostly done for a Long time but were missing a few key elements such as final audio. I've been holding off adding them as a way of adding new content to the game when its needed but it felt best to add them now to help with balancing the changes to challenges.

There is still a lot to do with the bears, mainly to figure out exactly what the reward/drive is for beating them. E.G maybe it will be a new armour type, a bag expansion or both that can be crafted from only their leather/fur. The time spent here will be in balancing the new items as well as making icons etc for them. 

[h3]Challenges[/h3]
The biggest change here is that challenges will become infinite waves with leaderboards, something I've wanted them to be from the start. This means that their rewards will instead be earned by reaching a high enough wave and that Tech Tokens can be earned in a slightly more consistent way instead of only being able to achieve a set amount.

The foundations for how these waves will function seems to be working well but its going to take plenty of time to balance the system to make sure its fair/fun.

[h3]Jungles[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/e96e29f7b8e762d8ed7837f07f7879bf656b0ca8.png[/img]
The first pass of jungles seems to be performing well so they are in and ready to explore. Here you can fight Panthers which in the end I decided to make identical to the Lioness in terms of stats and what is dropped.

I decided this was better than adding new items such as Panther leather because Lions are already rare as it is so it felt like having another way to find Lion Leather Strips etc would feel better than having another rare item/animal to grind.

[h3]Achievements UI[/h3]
This screen has been completely reworked in an effort to support controllers. Previously it used the same logic as the perks/talent trees because a few Achievements worked as a chain. E.G you had to equip all Copper tools before you could unlock the Tin tools achievement.

In hindsight, these chains didn't add enough value to the game so they have been removed, which allowed me to simplify the UI and start adding controller support to it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/898a2cf3cfa2dd3d6283d81b5a6c27d29a47f359.png[/img]

Mining stone has been rebalanced so that it should feel quicker to get through it all. Initially I kept it high to make room for future updates, such as the smeltery, new ores and advanced tools. However its feeling like this decision is generating too much tedium in the early game.

[h3]Challenges[/h3]
Challenges have been updated so that any destroyed blocks will automatically get a blueprint. Then once the challenge is over, you can walk over any blueprints and it will rebuild those missing blocks for you.

This was to prevent/reduce any frustration of building a base only for it to take damage and need rebuilt each time you take on a challenge.

[h3]Backups[/h3]
Each time you load a world or sleep in a bed a backup save file will now be generated. You can see and load your backups from the Load World menu

notes.title: Progress Update: Jungles
notes.content:
Its been a while since the last patch, and will be a while before the next one lands, so I thought I would give a quick update.

I've spent a bit of time on a major performance overhaul but it turned out to be a non starter, it would have saved decent GPU time but it cost far more CPU time than I was expecting so I had to shelve it for now.

I did this as an attempt to get ready for if I do decide to support Steam Decks (still not sure) but in the meantime controller support is still always a good thing so I've been slowly adding it to different screens. I wont lie though, its tedius work so I'm tackling it in bits and pieces in an attempt to prevent burnout.

Whilst I was thinking about performance, Jungles are something that has always been on the back of my mind because a good jungle is a dense one, which is more expensive to render. So I've decided its time to stop worrying about them from a theoretical point of view and to start working on them so I can figure out just how tricky they are going to be.

So far, its been better than expected and here is a first look at them:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/645f31502476e766c35f8bcaee5f84461afe3f9d.png[/img]

This is still heavily WIP but the foundations are feeling decent. Once I get the visuals nailed then a lot of the time spent will be on their economy. E.G do trees drop new wood, which enemies do you fight (its looking like Panthers) and thus what do they drop.

A new wood type will be a significant time sink since it means adding new variants for each relevant block, such as chests, fences, doors, planks etc etc etc. I've been developing tools to help make these changes easier/more automatic but its still a lot of settings and such to test.

If Panthers turn out well as a new enemy, I will probably also add some new challenges for them.

Finally I'm always working on bugs and have a fair few fixes built up ready for the next release. Although one I couldn't get to the bottom of involved a world corruption so I've been working on a backup system that will let you revert your worlds to the last few times you loaded them. Currently you can make backups yourself by exporting worlds but this system will instead automatically make a backup each time you load a world. I'm also hoping I can hook it up to key points in the game such as each time you sleep or die

notes.title: Performance, Water and Lore
notes.content:
For anyone that isn't familiar with game development, this is how it typically plays out

[previewyoutube=AbSehcT19u0;full][/previewyoutube]
I'm still working towards the Smeltery (and have made progress on it behind the scenes) but I realised that the Lore screen is needed first because the tutorials for the Structure Builder system aren't very clear and the smeltery will use the structure builder to make your first one.

At the same time, I wanted to continue work from the last update on performance and finally get an optimisation in there that is a pretty big change, but doing so worked best with the more advanced water systems. More info below...

[h3]Lore Screen[/h3]
The Lore screen is like an in game Encyclopedia

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/d752123c2028312d55a601175c4902b5630696dc.png[/img]
You can now use it to keep track of which plants, animals etc you have found in what biomes so if you are trying to finish some of the achievements or are just trying to find that missing crop you can spot where you have yet to finish exploring.

Now that this screen is ready, crops will now use the Anti-Wiki feature so that they will spawn in different biomes per world. I wanted to do this before but it felt too tedious to keep track of where you found things without it.

*[b]Please Note[/b]*
The lore page wont show information until you gather things again. E.G you might have already found a red berry bush, but it wont show which biome you found it in until you harvest from that bush again.

[h3]Combined Meshes[/h3]
This is an optimisation I started working on a long time ago but could never get into a stable state. What it does is combine chunks together so that there are less things for your graphics card to render at once.

What this means is that if your graphics card was struggling, you will likely see a fairly decent FPS increase and hopefully be able to increase your chunk draw distance.

However what this means is that there are a lot more scenarios for me to track when it comes to updating a chunk and its more likely to see things like the wrong visuals as you are breaking/placing blocks which is why this update is on the beta branch only until I can confirm its working well.

[h3]Water[/h3]
Water was problematic for the combined meshes because it would need to spread to neighbouring chunks each time a chunk loaded. Without combined meshes, this extra cost is fine but with them it introduced a lot of processing work as chunks would combine and then uncombine too often.

So to fix this, I've turned on the more complex water systems and tweaked their performance. This is because these systems handle water meshing separately from the rest of the chunk so it can be safely ignored by the new combined mesh optimisation.

What this means is that water should now flow much more naturally and let you do things like break a hole at the bottom of a lake and it will slowly drain into caves etc.

[h3]Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] Drastically increased the stats of the Lioness so she is much more dangerous
[*] Increased how much meat cows drop
[*] Added stats for each food item eaten
[*] Added various new buffs that are available for cooked meals
[*] Reduced the specular power of tree leaves so they are less shiny
[*] Fixed the snow rabbit not dropping its specific cooking recipe
[*] Added a minor buff for eating any hot meal. E.G cooked meat
[*] Increased the max health of the Lava Lord
[*] Challenge rewards can now only be claimed if you have enough inventory space (to prevent losing the reward in the world)
[*] Toggled spells no longer earn experience just for being activated
[*] Sprint settings are now under the options screen as well as the controls screen
[/list]

[h3]Performance[/h3]
[list]
[*] Optimised when the Fish jobs run so they are less likely to cost time on the main thread
[*] Reworked how fish send data to the GPU to be more efficient (an optimisation of CPU time)
[*] Fixed greedy meshing not working, this should result in an overall FPS boost
[*] Optimised the time it takes to generate the full screen maps image (its better but still slow for Hugely explored maps)
[/list]

[h3]Dropped Changes[/h3]
I've known about some bugs for a while now about things like falling through steps if there isn't a block below them and if you run up steps really fast you can launch off the top of them.

I did attempt to tackle these issues but it turned into a massive time sink and more complex than expected so they had to be dropped (for now) to prevent further delaying this already overdue release.

[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]

notes.title: Combat and Stones Update
notes.content:
This update brings fairly significant changes to combat to act as a foundation to build upon in future updates. There are also two new spells, a new challenge, a summary of carried items on the HUD, a ton of bug fixes and new stone blocks. 

As a bit of an update on the roadmap, once this update makes its way to the main branch I plan to do a bit of a bug fixing pass and then move onto a QoL update for inventory to include things like having chests inventory be included when using crafting benches etc.

After that I was planning on tackling Milestones but I realised they will work best once the Smeltery is ready so I’m getting ready to work on that instead. As a bit of a heads up, that update will be pretty big and take me a few weeks.

Finally I just want to emphasise that combat still has a long way to go and close combat especially has lots of room to improve so this is in no way a definitive combat update and there will be more in the future.

[h3]Combat[/h3]
The concept of Armour and Magic Resist has been added to animals/enemies.

Enemies can also level up and the max potential level increases each time you complete a challenge for the first time. 

How items drop has changed so that higher level enemies have better chances of dropping rare loot, meaning items that would previously drop with a low chance might not drop at all for level 1 enemies. 

Overall, this should mean rarer items are easier to get once you complete enough challenges.

Two new spells have been added, the first is Consecrate Area which will slowly deal damage to all enemies in an area.

[previewyoutube=fzzA8WBBHT8;full][/previewyoutube]
The other is Rock Volley which is a cheap to cast, short cooldown spell that you can launch at long range

[previewyoutube=5JR674Pdp5A;full][/previewyoutube]
Finally you now have a Magic Resist stat that can be increased by crafting a Talisman. For now only one type of Talisman can be crafted but more will likely be added in the future.

[h3]New Blocks[/h3]
The stone tiles recipe has been enabled for everyone again except that it now requires cement to craft, which can be crafted from animal bones + sand.

The main change here is that you can now create different stone tile types, such as:

[list]
[*] Sandstone
[*] Marble
[*] Mountain Stone
[*] Orthoclase
[*] Gray Orthoclase
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/5c1dd5780f31ca5431454ebf9bb3e2de089eb1ea.png[/img]

Eventually I plan for these textures to be applied to all stone blocks but for now it’s only applied to:
[list]
[*] Tiles

[*] Fences
[*] Gates
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/7039ef1d80bb9bacb30bb96e53c295ae9780d240.png[/img]

[h3]Carried Items HUD Element[/h3]
A new element has been added to the HUD which will tell you the total number of carried items of any item you have gathered recently.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/8b174332aa176ce291d7ce69909e0f6a36e35470.png[/img]

[h3]Settings Screen[/h3]
The settings screen was starting to get cramped so its been redesigned so that adding new settings in the future is a bit easier

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/aec212919ddb2fd051554301ad5d1f9c950a7c2e.png[/img]
[h3]Chunk Corruption Bug[/h3]
This bug was big enough I wanted to single it out. If you have ever been able to see through the world, like so:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/4efafa901e306549596755d82c518868dd1b9191.jpg[/img]
Then hopefully this bug will no longer happen. It was the root cause of a few issues, such as getting stuck, and was happening due to bad timing of when threads finished their work. This made it a nightmare to track down!

Unfortunately though if you had seen these chunk corruptions and edited the chunk in any way, then the corruption has been saved in your world and will still appear

notes.title: Release 0.1.3.0
notes.content:
This release is a pretty major one for Aiyana but most of its content is unlikely to be reached within the time limit for the demo. It includes:

[list]
[*] The first additional world layer for The Lost Civilisation
[*] Protection beacons
[*] A foundation for multiplayer (Disabled)
[*] Significant performance improvements
[*] Main Menu rework
[/list]
[h3]The Lost Civilisation[/h3]
This is the first world layer within Aiyana. Once your Protection Beacon reaches a high enough level it will reward you with a portal that will take you there to give you a new world to explore, similar to how the Nether works in Minecraft.

This layer is still a work in progress and has a long way to go but enough of a foundation is there to let you explore.

By exploring this layer you have easier access to ores that are rare in the Overworld as well as some new ones. There are also 2 new enemies, with more to come later, and a placeholder boss to defeat.


[h3]Protection Beacons[/h3]
Protection Beacons can now be crafted and act as the heart of your base. They will prevent nearby enemies from spawning or attacking you whilst inside its boundaries.

Beacons can be upgraded by crafting/placing various blocks within its borders as well as investing resources.


[h3]Main Menu Rework[/h3]
The main menu has always been a bit problematic to maintain because it was a static scene, which means its visuals needed their own meshes and shaders to render properly and these would frequently break.

To fix this, the menu scene is now a world that generates on the fly so it uses all the same content. The advantage of this is that new menu scenes can now be made very easily and as such now you should see a variety of different scenes in the main menu.

This took significantly more time than expected but has also helped fix a lot of bugs around world layers, using portals or reloading worlds. What I’ve done is remove the concept of there being a menu and main ‘scene’. Scenes are a concept within Unity to help manage things easily.

However switching scenes can be extremely slow so by us now not using scenes when you load a world it can take less than a second on mid spec machines.

The tradeoff is that there is now a loading screen before you see the first menu scene as data is prepared to load a world.


[h3]Multiplayer[/h3]
Significant progress has been made to lay a foundation for multiplayer in the future and should everything go well multiplayer within Aiyana will be completely free since there would be no need for a dedicated server. Instead servers would be hosted as lobbies via Steam.

However, there is still a significant amount of work/testing to do and currently I’m aiming for Aiyana to be released in April. I’m not confident I can get multiplayer into a state I will be happy with for that time.

In fact I highly doubt multiplayer will be a day 1 release which is a real shame but after 9 years I have to pull the trigger eventually.


[h3]Lighting[/h3]
[list]
[*] Improved light spreading from torches
[*] Fixed an issue where you could see light leaking through the world at sun rise/set
[*] There are still a lot of issues with lighting that will be addressed in a future update
[*] Lighting has been remade to distinguish between natural and emissive light. Still heavily WIP but this improves lighting in some scenarios
[/list]

[h3]Performance[/h3]
This update has some significant performance gains in many ways. Hopefully things will be running smoother now and allow higher FPS for all machines.


[h3]World Shape Improvements[/h3]
A long-standing bug in Aiyana to do with missing faces has Finally been fixed. In doing so, the world should be a bit smoother and biomes should no longer leak their height slightly into their neighbours.


Alongside this, biome generation has been completely reworked. You should now see a much wider variety of biomes more consistently however this does come with the tradeoff of animals looking more out of place as they wander around.


[h3]Bugs[/h3]
[list]
[*] Running down steps should feel better and no longer cause you to take fall damage
[*] Various sources of inventory corruption have been fixed
[/list]

[h3]Improvements[/h3]
[list]
[*] Dust should be appearing much more consistently now
[*] Rain will spawn more particles and be more obvious its raining
[*] Music has been reworked so that tracks will never be interrupted for new ones
[*] Rain has been remade and should look much nicer
[*] Structure builder animations have been reworked to feel more satisfying
[*] Crops and bushes have been reworked to be more stable
[/list]

[h3]Spells[/h3]
[list]
[*] Hover spell has been reworked to be more intuitive and eventually let you fly
[*] Drain life has been rebalanced to make it feel a bit more satisfying
[*] Fixed not being able to see the visuals for the Find Death Urns spell
[*] Casting spells now consumes hunger
[*] Dash can no longer be used to ‘fly’
[/list]

[h3]Animals[/h3]
[list]
[*] Levitating animals should navigate the world better
[*] Reduced the chances of encountering a night rabbit
[*] Improved how animals swim/attack in water (especially the Corrupted Native)
[*] Reduced how often animals flinch
[*] Corrupted Natives run a bit quicker
[*] Animals should avoid trees again
[*] Added audio to a few animals/enemies that were missing it
[*] Chickens will now randomly drop eggs
[*] Most animals now have a rare chance of dropping a cooking recipe
[/list]

[h3]Balancing/Changes[/h3]
[list]
[*] The starting island no longer has the broken portal and no longer protects you from enemies spawning at night

[*] Green crystals now also reward a significant amount of mining exp
[*] Fixed sword swings not rewarding exp for the attack speed stat
[*] Fixed the attack speed stat not working
[*] Combat tree has been rebalanced to need less kills before you can unlock later perks
[*] Archery damage has been significantly reduced

[*] Overall a lot of changes have been made to balancing, especially around how experience is earned for spells
[*] Buckets have been added again, allowing you to move water in a primitive way
[*] Alchemy has a new feature where you can invest Magical Essence to reveal ingredient properties
[*] Fancy beds are now craftable
[/list]

[h3]Achievements & Perks[/h3]

notes.title: Update 1.2.2.6
notes.content:
Since the last release I’ve had to hot fix the build a number of times to fix some critical issues, mainly to do with corruptions of inventory.

It feels like things are stabilising again so these notes summarise those hotfixes as well as things that have been added along the way.

A Massive thanks/shout out to Palandus (Bone) on forums here for finding and reporting on these issues!


[h3]Lighting & Torches[/h3]
I’ve always tried to have Aiyana be its own beast and not do things just because other games in this genre do things a certain way. The use of torches is one of those situations.

I’ve had to begrudgingly admit though that there is too much power in the mechanics to place cheap torches to explore caves to ignore.

The held torch is still just as prominent in Aiyana but now you can also craft cheap torches from the usual wood + coal to explore caves easily.

notes.title: Update 1.2.0
notes.content:
Welcome to the patch notes for the biggest update Aiyana has ever had! Since the last patch I’ve brought someone onboard to help with the code workload and we have been Really busy getting everything ready for release.

There have been more than 600 new additions to the project for this update!

The biggest changes have been in the animals and the player. Both have been rewritten almost from scratch to help make future work with them easier as well as to drastically optimise some of their costs and address some of the major flaws in the previous versions.

As well as this we have many other major new features:

[h3][b]New Animals[/b][/h3]
Four new animals now appear in the world:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/14f1685fdbbed890351527bdb2e0cfdf2f5a42f3.png[/img]

We have also added logic for most animals to be able to swim

[h3][b]Portals Systems[/b][/h3]
The starting portal can now be repaired to teleport you somewhere in the world.

You can also discover new portals in the world and link them to each other to make exploring easier.

Each portal will have a chest nearby with some loot such as new cooking recipes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/b12bfbae126d89ff4d01a5401b031405050ecff5.png[/img]

[h3][b]Map Updates[/b][/h3]
Instead of having to craft a cartography kit the map is now always available by pressing M.

Its UI  has been updated to include a legend of icons to help find points of interest in the world as well as be pannable and zoomable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/8791c6bdce86c9db6ab24c20edf4ff2a0a6f7dca.png[/img]

[h3][b]Biome Updates[/b][/h3]
The formulas for spawning biomes have been reworked so it’s much easier to find the more interesting biomes such as the swamps and savannah.

Swamps have also been overhauled to look much more swamp like
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/d566d8eaf86d0c609d35f119b13b0ce4ee6f3b0f.png[/img]

[h3][b]Auto Sorting Inventory & Multiple Hot Bars[/b][/h3]
The inventory has been updated to sort anything dropped into it automatically so that you don’t have to.

[previewyoutube=vA0HwxPCDBs;full][/previewyoutube]

Alongside this new perks have been introduced to have multiple hot bars to save you constantly having to go into main inventory.

[previewyoutube=cT9S1d7bKjY;full][/previewyoutube]

[h3][b]Performance[/b][/h3]
Performance has been drastically improved in all areas. CPU time has been reduced, we found and fixed a drastic use of memory that wasn’t intended. 

World loading algorithms have been remade to make world loading both quicker and smoother.

Finally GPU rendering time has been reduced by replacing old point light systems with more efficient versions.


[h3][b]Structure Builder[/b][/h3]
The structure builders interactions have been reworked to solve a few awkward scenarios as well as to make planning out a big structure more fun.

Now you can place blueprints in the world even if you don’t have the resources to build them, meaning you can plan out an area and the resources are taken from your inventory as you walk by.

[previewyoutube=8T5ZG-CrUh4;full][/previewyoutube]

There are also new UI options to expand the fencing of your building area without needing to remove your structure first.


[h3][b]Archery[/b][/h3]
Archery has been given a bit of an overhaul and things like quivers have been removed. Now firing a bow will fire arrows found automatically in your inventory.

The perk tree has also had a pass and is now fully functional. Some new perks include spells for improving your archery abilities.

The UI has been updated for whenever you hover over a bow or arrow to give you more information about its stats.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/8391e74ef5b58eb5f35957b7f4d9ba1db14557a1.png[/img]

Finally critical damage systems have been added and icons are shown whenever you get a crit.


[h3][b]New Objectives & Perks[/b][/h3]
The objectives have been reworked and new ones have been added to help explain more of the mechanics within Aiyana such as the structure builder.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/92b8b0fa7390ceb6473831306753776293d00f83.png[/img]

Perks have also been reworked and a new Crafting category has been added in order to make some of its perks more accessible and the exploring tree less sprawling.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/81b9234f54e0eca731fdab6db9ba7713623f530b.png[/img]
Alongside this some spells have been moved to be available as perks so they are easier to unlock such as Teleport Home, Dash and Detect Fish.

The perks screen has also been made pannable so it’s easier to use.

[h3][b]Fences & Signs[/b][/h3]
Fences have been given a quality of life pass so they now join to walls and each other in a way that looks more natural.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/7e77c3874f58e05a1778001c2bcf31958ade55f3.png[/img]

Signs have been reworked so if you place one on a wall it will turn into a wall sign that looks more sensible to be hanging there.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41141580/af056c1cbbea4a58a4c6c2f539cce99aa7b15b2c.png[/img]

[h3][b]Misc Additions & Changes[/b][/h3]
[list]
[*] The day & night durations have been changed to be longer
[*] Cloud shadows have been reworked to be much fainter which should make the world feel much brighter
[*] Pickups will now float in water so they are easier to gather
[*] Settings for a max fps of 72 and 90 have been added. These are more likely to introduce tearing if you select an option that is too high for your setup and is a scenario we hope to improve in the future
[*] Added a new setting to disable tutorials
[*] Water visuals have been improved so it’s easier to spot the water surface. There is more work we want to do here but it’s complex so we have left it as a lower priority until we fix some more important features
[*] Wooden tools have been added back into the game
[*] Drain Life spell now has targeting visuals so it’s easier to see when it should work
[*] The placing blocks system has been improved to feel more responsive by removing the previous placement animation
[*] Experience pickups are now more obvious with an extra icon to explain what you are picking up and how much of a reward each is
[*] Crafting UI has been reworked a bit so search is more obvious and the ‘All’ category is the default. The groups have also been further refined in an attempt to make things easier to navigate
[*] New settings for anti-aliasing have been added to the performance options screen
[/list]


[b][h3]Bug Fixes[/h3][/b]
So, so, so, so many bugs fixed but don’t worry we also made plenty more

notes.title: First Ever Update!

Hello all and welcome to the first ever patch notes for Aiyana! Its a pretty long and unexciting one that mainly tries to address all the feedback I've received so far, thank you again to everyone that has submitted any feedback reports.

Now that a lot of this is out of the way it should make future updates far more frequent.

I still have some open issues that I am struggling to track down or yet to tackle (invisible blocks, flying fish etc) but hopefully this update addresses most of the feedback received so far.

[b]Functionality Changes [/b]
[list]
[*] Reworked jump to feel less floaty, feel more responsive and sensibly account for players who hold jump in mid air
[*] Reduced fall damage to compensate
[*] Seaweed can no longer be placed on land
[*] Fixed the point where you are considered to be underwater so its more accurate
[*] Saplings now take far longer to turn into trees
[*] The fishing spear is now affected by the fishing stat so it is thrown further, more accurately etc
[*] Removed the wings from protection totems
[*] Reduced the intensity of the low health overlay so it's easier to see
[*] Increased the spawn rate of berry and cotton bushes in the world
[*] Improved the placing animation for flowers and grass
[*] Improved the starting portal flowers
[*] Improved grass bending so it bends multiple blocks at once and feels better moving diagonally
[*] Updated the bending of ferns to be nicer
[*] Removed excess foliage from the dark oak forest that was originally added as a testing ground
[*] Optimised seaweeds shaders
[*] Removed the can’t interact feedback audio when you try to place at your feet
[*] Updated achievements around sleeping so don't dont get two at once for doing one thing
[*] Reworked dust to use proper GPU Instancing instead of being limited to 1024 per batch
[*] Reworked the visuals and density of dust
[*] Updated rain so it fades out more smoothly
[*] Added a fading system so rain is less intrusive in front of the players face but is nice and visible in the distance
[*] Optimised world colliders
[*] Added new systems to allow certain blocks to render with GPU instancing automatically
[*] Ensured the clouds job is running with Burst
[*] Updated the logic behind crafting to auto select the material you have the most of when you are carrying many different types (E.G carrying 2 types of wood)
[*] Fixed a bug that would leave the eating UI stuck on screen
[*] Fixed some bugs that would cause the camera to be stuck in an off position after interacting with a crafting bench
[*] Ensured that secondary prefabs where being handled properly (this was causing insect wings to not always render)
[*] Changed the tutorials so if they point at a button, pressing the button will also close the tutorial instead of being non responsive
[*] Removed extra health bar visuals since it caused confusion

[*] Increased the min scale of sea shells on the starting island
[*] Wolves will attack the player quicker if they interrupt their howl
